::: {#about-block}
Dr. Colin Kuehl is an Associate Professor in the Department of [Political Science](www.polisci.niu.edu) and [Institute for the Study of the Environment Sustainability and Energy](https://www.niu.edu/clas/ese/index.shtml) at [Northern Illinois University](www.niu.edu) where he is also affiliated with the [Center for Southeast Asian Studies](https://www.niu.edu/clas/cseas/index.shtml).



Dr. Kuehl's scholarship focuses on the politics of environmental behavior. He researches broad questions across different political domains and levels of analysis, from motivating individuals to conserve water to what makes countries more likely to ratify multi-lateral environmental agreements, using a wide variety of methodological approaches. His work has been published in [Environmental Politics](https://doi.org/10.1080/09644016.2025.2604372), [Nature Sustainability](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41893-021-00687-6), [The Journal of Policy Analysis and Management](https://huskiecommons.lib.niu.edu/niubib/526/), [Science Communication](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/10755470231153634), and other highly regarded outlets. He is currently working on a book project focused on individual attitudes toward global environmental cooperation.

For the Spring 2026 semester he was a Visiting Scholar at Northwestern University Department of Political Science and Summer 2026 he was a Visiting Professor at the School of Public Policy at Chiang Mai University in Thailand.

Colin was born and raised in small-town northeast Oregon and received his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara in 2017. In his free time he likes to drink coffee, watch soccer (#ynwa), and go on road trips with his wife, two daughters, and dog.
:::
